ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory Client Due Diligence (CDD) on the founder, foundation council members, protector, and all named beneficiaries. Residents agents and applicable financial institutions must screen against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT, and Panamanian national/UAF alert lists. PEP status (domestic or foreign) triggers Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) with senior-management approval under Ley 23/2015 and SBP Acuerdo 4-2022. Source of funds and source of wealth are verified at formation for the ISIC 3250 dialysis-hemofilter manufacturing project. Foundation risk tier: Low_Risk_Standard, with annual re-verification of UBO data in the RBF-DGI registry.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Registro en Línea (online name search and reservation portal); official site: https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names must be rendered in the Spanish/Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are not accepted in the Panama Public Registry and must be transliterated. The foundation name may be phrased in Spanish or a foreign language in Latin script and must end with 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'F.I.P.' (alternatively 'Private Interest Foundation') to distinguish it from a trading corporation or public-benefit foundation. The name must not be identical, orthographically, or phonetically confusingly similar to any name already registered in the Registro Público.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are valid for 30 calendar days and are not statutorily extendable; if the reservation lapses, the applicant must re-file with a new search fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) obtain the written reason from the Registo Público legal department; (ii) file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Director General del Registro Público within 5 business days under Ley No. 38 de 2000; (iii) on second denial, file a 'Recurso de Apelación' before the same authority for hierarchical exhaustion, followed by judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months. Practically, for medical-adjacent tokens such as 'Diálisis' or 'Clínica', prior written authorization from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA/DIGESA) is recommended before filing to avoid rejection, and a modified name may be re-filed immediately in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted — the PIF must appoint a resident agent that is a Panama-licensed attorney or licensed law firm maintaining a physical operating office in Panama; the registered office of the foundation is the resident agent's physical address. A standalone virtual-mailbox address without an attorney-agent's physical office does not satisfy Ley No. 25 de 1995 or current Registro Público practice. A cloud/virtual service layered on top of the licensed agent's physical office is tolerated for administrative convenience but does not replace the statutory domicile requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% annual probability of unannounced inspection of a low-risk holding PIF's registered office by UAF/DGI in the current post-FATF-grey-list supervisory environment; moderate (approximately 25-35%) for the underlying ISIC 3250 manufacturing subsidiary, which is subject to MINSA/DIGESA health-establishment inspections and product-quality supervision for medical devices and dialysis consumables.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Law 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations) as amended by Law 13 of 2013, Articles 1, 2, 4-8, 26-30 and 40-43
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Foundation Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundación / Acta de Constitución (Foundation Charter)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Foundation Charter must state the initial endowment, which must be adequate for the foundation's purposes. Endowment funds may be held in escrow at a Panamanian financial institution and released upon registration of the Charter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned members of the Foundation Council, duly appointed by the Founder under the Foundation Charter, hereby resolve: (1) The initial endowment is accepted and fully subscribed by the Founder. (2) The registered office is fixed at the address of the Registered Agent in Panama City, as designated in the Charter. (3) The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer, each empowered to act for routine administrative acts. (4) The President is instructed to effect all post-registration filings, including tax registration and municipal licensing, and to open the corporate bank account. Approved on this date at Panama City.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foundation Charter Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Reservation Portal (Ventanilla Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish, including the foundation name, initial endowment, council members, registered agent, and purposes. Submit a name reservation request online; upon approval, print the reserved name certificate and schedule notarization.
required_dossiers: Copy of Founder's passport and proof of legal capacity
Home address and contact details of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, modify the proposed name and resubmit a new reservation request; if charter deficiencies are flagged, correct and re-submit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (licensed Panamanian notary) / Registered Agent (any attorney or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary. The notary will verify identity of the founder, record the charter in the protocol, and issue a notarized copy. The registered agent of record must accept the position and execute the acceptance.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founder and council members
Proof of payment of notary and legal fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires supplementary documentation, supply the requested items within one week and reschedule the protocol signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicios Externos / Registry Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter to the Public Registry with the required number of certified copies and the tax fee receipt. The Registry examines the Charter for compliance with Law 25; upon approval, it records the charter and issues irrevocable registry certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original and two certified copies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an observation list, respond with a corrected charter or legal brief curing the deficiency; a formal 'Vista Fiscal' opinion may be requested if contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance and Registered Office Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, adopt the first board resolution as provided, prepare the minutes of the initial council meeting, and adopt the bylaws or internal regulations. The registered office is the address set out in the charter; confirm written acceptance. Issue officer appointment certificates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes are challenged by any member, ratify them in a subsequent extraordinary council meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Panama National Tax Administration / Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the foundation's Tax Identification Number (RUC) by filing the constituent documents with DGI. Register the establishment for municipal business tax (Aviso de Operación) before the Municipality of Panama. This also enables bank account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requires additional supporting documents, submit the requested items within the specified filing window and check the electronic portal for filed notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Sanitary License Application for Medical Device Manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the sanitary registration application for the disposable dialysis hemofilter as a Class II/III medical device, together with the manufacturing establishment license request. Site inspection by MINSA will be scheduled; production may not commence until license is issued.
required_dossiers: Technical device file (ITS, ISO 13485 documentation if applicable)
Facts of manufacturing facility and equipment list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the sanitary application is queried, respond with a technical supplement within 15 days; a new inspection may be arranged.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for industrial establishment registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos and Licencia de Operación para Establecimiento Fabricante de Dispositivos Médicos

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio del Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Requerido for small-to-medium scale manufacturing facilities; simplified EIA for facilities below 10,000 m² under the national schedule
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial effluent limits per DGNTI-COPANIT 22 (BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L); VOCs from solvent use must be controlled using wet scrubbers or carbon adsorption, and air emissions must comply with DGNTI-COPANIT National Air Quality Rules; hazardous waste disposal shall conform to MiAMBIENTE's waste regulation 14/2015.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load inspection from the Municipality of the site; workplace safety clearance from MINSA – Dirección General de Salud / Occupational Health Inspectorate and compliance with mandatory occupancy permit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), attached to the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of Panama; electronic taxpayer portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (Sede Electrónica / SITA system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned PIF obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by: (1) filing the foundation’s charter and registered agent certificate with the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) legalizing/apostilling and providing official Spanish translation when foreign incorporation is involved; (3) presenting the RUC application to the DGI via the taxpayer portal or agency window together with the foundation’s bylaws, certificate of existence and a designation of local fiscal representative; (4) paying the applicable Registry and DGI fees; and (5) receiving the RUC certificate and, if taxable supplies will be made, the ITBMS (VAT) account. Non-resident entities without a PE register expediently for ITBMS purposes only, using a temporary non-resident RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Panamanian law; classification follows statutory legal form and activity. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) may, however, elect its operating posture: (a) remain a passive asset-holding foundation with no Panamanian-source commercial activity, which keeps it outside entity-level income tax and ITBMS; or (b) register its Panamanian-source commercial activity (manufacturing, invoicing, shipments) and thereby become an entity-level territorial taxpayer subject to ISR and ITBMS. The Foundation may also designate in its bylaws that its assets are used only for the purposes described in its deed, which affects DGI characterization and the availability of the annual flat foundation fee.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), equal to VAT/GST in scope and operation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 (no threshold once any taxable Panamanian-source supply is made); small-taxpayer simplified regime threshold: B/. 36,000 annual gross turnover. Non-residents supplying into Panama must register for ITBMS in the same manner as residents when their actions are performed in Panama or the taxable act is to be used in Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic fiscal invoicing ('Facturación Electrónica DGI') for all registered ITBMS taxpayers. Invoices must be generated through the DGI-approved fiscal channel (web portal or certified ERP API) and obtain real-time DGI authorization/clearing before delivery to the buyer. Each invoice must contain a DGI digital stamp, GUID/folio, QR code and the taxpayer’s RUC. Export invoices must identify the customs export declaration and are cancellable only with customs exit evidence. Failure to clear electronically renders the invoice invalid, disallows the buyer’s input-credit and exposes the seller to fiscal-infraction fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate, provided the exporter holds a valid RUC/ITBMS registration, has obtained the definitive export authorization from the Panamanian customs authority (ANA) and retains evidence of territorial exit. Offshore services, and services rendered outside Panama to non-residents, are also treated as non-Panamanian-source and are excluded from ITBMS (zero-rated) when the beneficiary and place of consumption are abroad. The rate also extends to construction and repair services on vessels/aircraft used in international traffic and to goods entered into Colon Free Zone operatives when the physical removal to foreign territory is demonstrated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera, DUA) approved by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), showing the exported product classification and destination.
Bill of Lading (ocean/air/international modal transport document) evidencing actual physical departure from Panamanian territory to the overseas consignee.
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate evidencing deposit/credit of the export sales proceeds to a Panamanian bank account, where proceeds repatriation is contractually required).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is scrutinized against DUA, transport, bank, and insurance records. If the DGI or ANA determines that an export was fictitious, misdescribed, or that the goods did not leave Panama, the exporter is retroactively assessed the unpaid 7% ITBMS, with late interest, and subject to a monetary surcharge of 25%–75% of the omitted tax (higher when fraud is proven). Fraudulent zero-rating may also trigger criminal tax-fraud liability, customs seizure, suspension of the issuer’s electronic-invoice authorization, cancellation of the RUC, and an extended audit limitation period of up to seven years in cases of scheme/fraud. Refunds already paid can be clawed back, with statutory interest running from the date of the false refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without an independent central bank or monetary authority. The Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá - SBP) is the sole banking, AML/CFT, and financial-system supervisor under Decree Law 9 of 1998, as amended by Law 79 of 2020. Banco Nacional de Panamá, the state-owned commercial bank, acts as fiscal agent and clearing agent for the central government but possesses no exchange-control or currency-issuance powers. There is therefore no Central Bank FX window, no prior-approval mechanism for foreign investment, and no exchange-rate policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility under a completely dollarized economy. The Panamanian balboa (PAB) exists solely in metallic coinage at a fixed 1:1 legal parity with the U.S. dollar (USD), which constitutes the entire paper-money base and legal tender for all transactions. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully open, with no restrictions on inflow, outflow, lending, repatriation, or pricing of foreign exchange. For the PIF's dialysis-hemofilter export business, profit remittance is entirely free in USD. Panama applies a territorial tax system: the 10% dividend/distribution tax applies only to profits derived from Panama-source income; export-derived proceeds are exempt Panama-source income and may be remitted to non-resident beneficiaries without additional tax withholding, provided the entity maintains clean transfer-pricing and substance documentation under Law 254 of 2021.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No compulsory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline exists for export proceeds. Exporters may retain 100% of export receipts in USD or any other convertible currency held in Panamanian or offshore bank accounts. Regulatory obligations are limited to (i) MINSA/DIGESA sanitary registration of the medical device, (ii) filing of the export customs declaration through the SIMDA single-window system, and (iii) retention of the export invoice, bill of lading, and purchase order in the trade dossier for bank and tax audit purposes. None of these documents triggers a foreign-exchange conversion or timeline-based surrender event.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Panama's Law 112 of 2023 establishes an SBP-regulated Fintech Sandbox but does not create an EU-style electronic-money institution (EMI) license; locally licensed sandbox firms may perform pilot payment activities with reduced capital during a 12–36-month window. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer) frequently decline Panamanian Private Interest Foundations due to the foundation's private bylaws and the absence of a conventional shareholding register for automated beneficial-ownership extraction. Legal constraint: if an offshore EMI lands in Panama, executes payments on behalf of the entity to Panamanian counterparties, or holds funds in custody, it must obtain SBP authorization; failure to do so shifts tax and regulatory risk to the PIF. Recommended architecture: use the tier-1 Panamanian bank as the principal treasury account and employ the EMI strictly as a pass-through collection rail for export invoices, with the EMI contract explicitly stating it is not a Panamanian-constituted deposit-taking intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP Rule 52-2020 does not mandate a face-to-face interview as a categorical requirement, but the internal CDD policies of virtually all tier-1 Panamanian banks require an in-person or high-assurance video interview for a non-resident-owned PIF. Practical mandate: at least one executive or beneficial owner must complete a live video interview with the bank's compliance officer, presenting a valid passport and proof of address, while the Panama Resident Agent simultaneously executes a notarized power of attorney granting express powers to operate the account, waive banking secrecy, and receive compliance requests. This dual structure satisfies the 'on-site representative' requirement. Full remote opening without a resident-agent power of attorney and without a banker's reference letter from a reputable correspondent bank is not available at the tier-1 institutions listed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner holds citizenship or tax residence in a jurisdiction classified by the SBP or FATF as high-risk, or the owner's name appears on sanctions logs at screening stage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified tax-residence certificate; 3 months of personal bank statements from a regulated financial institution; sworn declaration of source of wealth; output of an independent commercial sanctions-screening report documenting a negative match; evidence that the dialysis-filter commercial counterparties are solely regulated hospital distributors and public health ministries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the PIF Charter's stated estate-planning or asset-protection purpose and the proposed active manufacturing business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended Foundation Charter and Bylaws (Reglamento) explicitly authorizing 'manufacture, distribution, and international sale of medical devices and renal-dialysis consumables'; ISO 13485 quality-management certificate; MINSA/DIGESA sanitary registration for the hemofilter; floor plan and purchase orders for the extrusion and potting line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure or delay in filing the Beneficial Ownership Return with the Public Registry, creating a compliance red flag under Law 129 of 2020 and GAFILAT-style inspections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Updated Beneficial Ownership issued by the Registro Público de Panamá; a foundation-council resolution identifying the founder, council members, and protector as subject persons; notarized consent letters from each beneficial owner authorizing disclosure to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of nominee or professional Foundation Council members giving rise to a perceived concealment of the true economic controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed and undated irrevocable letters of resignation from each nominee council member; non-debt-acceptance letters; a resolutive-condition mandate with an unremovable revocation clause; full biographical data of the nominated council members; an explanation of the commercial rationale for appointing a professional council.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, round-number USD wire traffic inconsistent with a low-risk medical-device exporter's cash-flow patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the underlying export contract with the foreign hospital group or government procurement agency; commercial invoices referencing hemofilter model numbers and membrane pore-size specs; packing lists; bills of lading with matched Incoterms; customs export declarations; warehouse inventory records; and the treasury department's documented funding schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) The sending institution executes an SWIFT MT103 with Beneficiary as the PIF's exact registered name and account; Field 50K must name the overseas funder; Field 56A must identify the sending bank's New York correspondent (e.g., JPMorgan or BofA); Field 70 must clearly state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – PIF ENDOWMENT INCREASE – NON-COMMERCIAL REMITTANCE'. (2) No mandatory pre-registration exists in Panama, but the PIF's tax file at the DGI must reconcile the credit to the Foundation's General Ledger under 'Paid-in Endowment'. (3) The bank will request a Council Resolution approving the capital increase, the Good Standing Certificate from the Public Registry, and the Updated Beneficial Ownership Certificate before final crediting; upon credit, the PIF treasurer must issue a notarized acknowledgment letter and file an amended note to the Foundation's asset schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) For open-account procurement of polyethersulfone (PES) resin, tubing, and packaging: SWIFT MT103 via the tier-1 bank's New York correspondent; the beneficiary bank must receive an original-compliant CTC payment order, commercial invoice, packing list, and pre-shipment inspection certificate when required. (2) For high-value extrusion and potting machinery imports: irrevocable, confirmed 90-day-sight commercial Letter of Credit issued under SWIFT MT700/MT707, with the beneficiary bank in the EU or Japan; documentation includes the bill of lading, commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and full warranty protocols. (3) For settlements in Chinese Renminbi with PRC raw-material suppliers: route through the CIPS-CHIPS/SWIFT parallel chain using an MT103 equivalent with reference 'TT FOR TRADE SETTLEMENT'; Panamanian banks apply no limit on CNY conversion or settlement. (4) For export collections from MENA or LAC public-health buyers: documentary collection D/P or D/A plus standby LC; for larger tenders, the Panamanian bank confirms the import LC and forwards the shipping set directly to the confirming bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC USD/EUR deliverable outright forwards, booked with an SBP-supervised treasury desk and settled through the bank's New York correspondent
Offshore USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for Renminbi procurement flows, executed by the Panamanian bank's treasury unit with a top-tier Chinese or Hong Kong bank as pricing counterparty

USD/JPY and USD/EUR cross-currency basis swaps for fixed-asset CapEx financing of imported extrusion and potting machinery, under an SBP-recognized International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA 2002) master agreement approved by the Foundation Council
European-style currency options (USD/EUR) for hedging invoice exposure on competitive-currency export tenders, subject to the bank's credit-risk committee approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Matrícula renewal payment for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March under the calendar-year rule; no separate annual return is required for a passive foundation without Panama-source commercial activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers statutory late-payment penalties and interest; continued default deprives the foundation of good standing before the Public Registry, blocks issuance of registry certificates, and may ultimately lead to administrative suspension or strike-off of the foundation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to a passive Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. Mandatory audited financial statements may be required by the DGI only when the foundation carries on Panama-source taxable commercial activity, in which case the taxation and audit determination follows the Panamanian Fiscal Code rather than a fixed PIF-specific numerical threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs may be applied to qualifying small entities; statutory fiscal bookkeeping follows the Panamanian Fiscal Code where the foundation becomes an active taxpayer

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama private interest foundations have no annual UBO filing requirement. The registered agent maintains a confidential beneficial-owner record and conducts a written annual confirmation from the Foundation Council, normally aligned with the 31 March Matrícula renewal, verifying that there has been no change in beneficiaries, council members, or protectors. Any transfer or substitution of beneficiaries or council membership must be reflected in the foundation records and, where required, reported to the Public Registry within 30 days of the event under Law 129 of 2020.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (director register equivalent)
Confidential Beneficiaries Register (members register equivalent for UBO maintenance)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–900 per year for a Panama resident agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–5,000 if a local DGI or third-party financing audit becomes necessary; USD 0 for a fully passive foundation with no audit trigger

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat corporate income tax on net taxable income derived from Panamanian sources under the territorial income tax system (Código Fiscal, Ley 77 de 1956 as amended). Income sourced outside Panama, including export manufacturing sales, is outside thePanamanian tax net.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effectively 0% Panamanian CIT on foreign-source export profits where the manufacturing and sale occur predominantly outside Panamanian territory. Panama-Pacifico Special Economic Zone qualifying manufacturing operators may obtain a CIT exemption through 2027 and a reduced 5% rate thereafter. Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) under Law 25 of 1995 are not taxed on foreign-source income and distributions of non-Panamanian patrimony are not subject to income tax. No general tax holiday for ISIC 3250 production, but duty drawback and Law 69 industrial exemptions apply to imported dialysis-membrane inputs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 102 (Declaración Anual de Renta para Personas Jurídicas / Sociedades) filed electronically by the resident agent or legal representative through the DGI e-filing platform 'E-Tax 2.0' (Sistema PATRON). Quarterly advance payments filed on Formulario 106. Monthly withholding and ISD reports filed on Formulario 108/110 where applicable. Audited financial statements must be attached when annual gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual Form 102; quarterly advance payments (Form 106) for taxpayers with gross annual revenue above USD 1,500,000; monthly withholding, payroll, and advance dividend tax (ISD) filings for distributing or employing entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 102 must be filed no later than 31 March following the fiscal year end (three months after close of the calendar year). A discretionary extension of up to two months may be requested from the DGI before the original due date; the extension does not postpone payment of assessed tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross sales, service fees, and other revenues effectively derived from economic activity located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF manufacturing dialysis consumables for export: report only revenues from sales consummated in Panama or from services rendered in Panama. Export sales to US/EU/LATAM distributors are not reported here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 2 – Devoluciones y rebajas sobre ventas (returns and rebates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales returns, discounts, rebates, and allowances directly linked to Panamanian-source sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduces Línea 1. For export sales, show returns in a separate support schedule; not deductible against non-taxed foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 4 – Ingresos exentos y rentas de fuente extranjera (exempt and foreign-source income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on foreign deposits, foreign royalties, dividends from non-Panamanian subsidiaries, and all profits from operations located abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Critical line for the PIF: every dollar of foreign-source export profit and foreign dividend must be declared here to preserve exemption. Attach a sworn statement and underlying contracts/invoices to avoid recharacterization as Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 9 – Costo de ventas y gastos deducibles (cost of sales and deductible expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses causally connected to Panamanian-source income; inventory costs for goods sold in Panama, wages of Panamanian plant staff, local utilities, lease of Panamanian facilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not commingle Panamanian and foreign-source expenses. Expenses matched to foreign-source revenue are not deductible from Panamanian taxable income but reduce the foreign-source surplus distributable without withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 14 – Renta neta gravable (net taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source gross revenue minus permitted deductions; 0.00 for a fully export-oriented PIF after proper reporting of Línea 4, but the line remains mandatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the DGI detects unallocated cost pools shifting profits from Panamanian activity to the foreign pool, this line is recalculated under transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 17 – Impuesto sobre la renta determinado (25% of Línea 14)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax assessed on Panamanian-source net income at 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expected to be zero for a clean PIF without Panamanian-source transactions; any positive amount triggers advance dividend tax analysis for future distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 19 – Créditos por retenciones y pagos a cuenta (credits for withholding and advance payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Form 106 quarterly prepayments, third-party withholdings, and foreign tax credits only for reclassified Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax credit is generated by foreign withholding taxes on export sales because no Panamanian tax is assessed on that pool; do not enter foreign taxes here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cuadro 22 / Anexo de Precios de Transferencia
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn statement and disclosure annex covering all transactions with related parties, residents of low-tax jurisdictions, and the PIF's connected entities; required whenever the taxpayer exceeds annual revenue or related-party transaction thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with zero Panama-source income must nevertheless disclose any intercompany purchases/sales of dialysis filter membranes from/to affiliates. Failure to attach the annex voids the benefit of the territorial exemption for the covered transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 102 incurs a surcharge of 5% per month or fraction of a month on the tax due, capped at 50%; a fixed administrative fine of USD 500 applies to failure to file a zero-tax return; late payment interest accrues at 1% per month (12% annual) on the unpaid balance; formal-obligation fines range from USD 100 to USD 25,000 depending on gravity; continued non-compliance may trigger temporary business closure and cancellation of the RUC tax registry number.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends distributed from net income subject to Panamanian-source taxation (Código Fiscal on dividends). Dividends and PIF distributions paid out of non-Panamanian, foreign-source patrimony are subject to 0% Panamanian withholding. Treaty-resident corporate shareholders holding at least 10% may benefit from a reduced withholding rate of 5% where a Double Tax Agreement applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Administrative protocol: (1) confirm that the recipient is fiscally resident in a treaty jurisdiction, including Barbados, Republic of Korea, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, Spain, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom; (2) obtain from the recipient's home tax authority a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued for the current calendar year and, at the payor's request, an apostilled copy; (3) before the payment date, submit the TRC together with the Panamanian sworn application (Formulario 140 / Declaración Jurada para aplicación de convenios) to the paying PIF or company; (4) withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after validating the TRC and the applicant's entitlement; (5) retain the TRC, the sworn declaration, and underlying ownership evidence for at least five years for DGI inspection. An expired or missing TRC obliges the payor to apply the statutory 10% rate and exposes the payor to surcharge liability for under-withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident banks and lenders on external financing: 0% statutory withholding as non-Panamanian-source income. Interest paid to non-resident financial institutions for onshore Panamanian loans remains generally exempt in line with territoriality. Royalties and technical assistance fees for the economic use of trademarks, patents, or know-how inside Panama: statutory withholding at 12.5%; treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 5–10% where a DTA applies. Royalties for exploitation of IP outside Panama: 0% withholding, provided the IP contract records the geographic field of use and the payor maintains exit-tax diligence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,500,000 (Balboa parity) in annual gross revenue is the general threshold triggering the mandatory transfer pricing sworn declaration and contemporaneous Local File. Separate mandatory documentation is required where annual related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000, even if total revenue is below USD 1,500,000. Multi-national groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000 must file Country-by-Country Reports through the DGI under Panama's OECD BEPS minimum standards (Law 23 of 2015 provisions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the UAE/BVI type for ordinary PIFs, but the territorial tax regime applies a de facto economic-situs test: profits attributed to foreign-source activity are exempt only if substantive activities (manufacturing, purchasing, invoicing, and decision-making) occur outside Panama. Panama-Pacifico and SEM preferential regimes are conditioned on headcount, local premises, and core-income-generating activities per OECD substantial-activity factor. A PIF with personnel, contracts, and bank accounts all in Panama and merely labeling income as 'foreign-source' risks recharacterization. Law 254 of 2021 strengthened transparency and beneficial-ownership reporting for foundations; entities with gross revenue above USD 3,000,000 must file DGI-audited financial statements, and any artificial structuring to avoid the USD 250,000 related-party threshold is an aggravating circumstance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally under-reporting Panamanian-source sales of dialysis consumables, fabricating export invoices to shift revenue into the foreign-source pool, destroying books, or filing false cost declarations with the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama Código Fiscal criminal tax fraud provisions (introduced by Law 38 of 2010): imprisonment of 2–5 years and a fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax; civil re-assessment of the full tax, monthly 12% annual interest, and late-filing surcharges of 5% per month capped at 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, financial officers, and the PIF council members who sign fraudulent returns are personally liable for civil restitution; the Public Ministry may issue travel bans (pedimento) and preventive detention; conviction triggers disqualification from holding office in Panamanian companies and full corporate-veil piercing against personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Private Interest Foundation as a bare-mailbox shareholder of the dialysis filter manufacturer with no staff, no premises, and no substance, while routing Panamanian manufacturing income through the foundation to create a false 'foreign-source' exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterizes the transaction under the real-economic-situs principle, taxes the hidden Panamanian beneficiary, and imposes the 50% penalty on the undeclared tax; failure to maintain accounting records at the registered office triggers administrative fines; repeated misuse may lead to court-ordered foundation dissolution and cancellation of the resident agent's license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Consejo de Fundación and protector owe fiduciary duties; fraudulent asset transfers make them personally liable to creditors and the DGI to the extent of assets transferred; criminal prosecution can follow under Law 70 of 2019 where the shell was used for laundering trade proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Sanctions Violations in Trade Finance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Swift LC or TT wire payments from hospital distributors located in sanctioned jurisdictions, structuring payments to avoid bank AML thresholds, or using unlicensed crypto-fintech rails to collect export proceeds while the PIF fails to register as a non-financial designated business or to file ROS (reporte de operaciones sospechosas) with the UAF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 (amended by Law 70 of 2019), administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation for legal persons; money-laundering penalties under the Código Penal of 5–10 years' imprisonment for the underlying predicate offence; DGI and UAF joint freezing of bank accounts and revocation of the RUC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute or authorize transfers to proscribed persons are subject to criminal liability; the UAF may place them on the politically exposed persons watchlist, impose travel bans, and recommend extradition under Panama's mutual legal assistance treaty with the United States; personal assets are reachable via criminal forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding, Social Security, and Advance Dividend Tax Abuses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring quarterly Form 106 prepayment and withholding returns but failing to remit the collected CSS payroll deductions of Panamanian factory employees, or never filing the ISD (advance dividend tax at 4%) while accumulating retained earnings from Panamanian operations in anticipation of a future tax-free PIF distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-remitted withholdings attract the 5%-per-month surcharge (capped at 50%) plus 12% annual interest; CSS crimes for conversion of employee payroll deductions expose the entity to fines up to USD 100,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years for repeat violations; the ISD delinquency blocks the issuance of solvency certificates and the ability to transfer company equity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers who knowingly divert withheld staff contributions are jointly and severally liable for the full shortfall; criminal prosecution by the Ministerio Público on complaint of CSS can result in preventive detention, professional disbarment, and personal bankruptcy orders for restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling finished hemofilters to a US/EU distribution affiliate at a recurrent loss while buying hollow-fiber membranes from another affiliated supplier above market, without a contemporaneous TP Study, and failing to attach the Anexo de Precios de Transferencia to Form 102.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may make a presumptive re-assessment using the highest-arm's-length comparable; the adjustment is subject to 12% annual interest and a 50% penalty on the recomputed tax; the taxpayer loses the loss-carryforward entitlements for the audited year; formal fines of USD 10,000–50,000 apply for the missing annex.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers are jointly liable for the 50% surcharge if the company is insolvent; the DGI sends the file to the Public Prosecutor for criminal tax fraud; a negative solvency certificate blocks the PIF from paying dividends, liquidating assets, or financing operations, and the resident agent may resign and trigger compulsory winding-up.
